BOOK GAP (book p.65, VSAQ 8): the printed answer is one line and never says that the solute must be NON-VOLATILE, never gives ΔTf = Kf m, never gives the unit K kg mol⁻¹, and never says that Kf is a property of the SOLVENT alone. All four are written here. The value Kf = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹ for water is added from the standard data table; it is not printed in this book. NOTATION: Kf is written with a plain small f because Unicode has no subscript f.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The cryoscopic constant, Kf, is the
depression of freezing point produced when
one mole of a non-volatile solute is
dissolved in 1000 g (one kilogram) of the
It is also called the molal depression
steps.why: One mole of solute in one kilogram of solvent is a one molal solution, so the definition is the value of ΔTf at m = 1. Fixing the amount this way makes Kf a single number for each solvent, which is what lets a measured ΔTf be turned into a molar mass.
common_mistakes: Writing 1000 g of SOLUTION. The definition uses 1000 g of solvent.
Saying the freezing point rises. A solute lowers the freezing point, so ΔTf is a depression.
steps.memory_tip: Cryo means cold, so Kf is the freezing point constant.
steps.margin_note: "One mole in 1000 g of solvent" is the marked phrase. Molal depression constant is the accepted second name.

steps.label: The equation and the unit
lines: Unit of Kf: K kg mol⁻¹
Kf is a property of the solvent alone. It
does not depend on the solute.
For water, Kf = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹.
steps.why: Depression of freezing point is a colligative property, so ΔTf depends only on the number of solute particles, measured as molality. Kf holds everything that belongs to the solvent — its freezing point and its enthalpy of fusion — so the same value is used for every solute dissolved in that solvent.
common_mistakes: Writing ΔTf = Kf M with molarity. The equation uses molality m.
Using Kf for an electrolyte without the van't Hoff factor. A solute that dissociates gives ΔTf = i Kf m.
steps.memory_tip: For water Kf = 1.86 and Kb = 0.52, so freezing is the larger effect.
steps.margin_note: The unit K kg mol⁻¹ and the "property of the solvent" line complete this mark.

insider_note: Kf for water, 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹, is larger than Kb, 0.52 K kg mol⁻¹. That is why molar masses are measured by freezing point in practice: the same solution gives a bigger temperature change to read.
